source.title: Computing the Testing Error Without a Testing Set
source.authors: C. Corneanu; M. Madadi; Sergio Escalera; Aleix M. Martinez

page_placements.theme: Representation geometry and topology provide conditional diagnostics

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether persistent-topology summaries predict the training–testing performance gap, using cross-validation and held-out datasets. This is a different measurement aimed at the gap, not a test of the claim’s listed mechanisms or sharpness measure.
record.gate_note: Reports the association between two topological summaries and the performance gap, plus prediction errors for the proposed estimator. It does not test memorization of random labels or the architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, model-size, dropout, adaptive-optimizer, or large-batch comparisons in V1–V6. Reported earlier findings in the related-work section are citations, not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether functional-topology summaries predict the generalization gap. None of V1–V8 names these summaries. In particular, it measures neither magnitude-aware weight sharpness nor its ranking against norm and margin measures, so its correlations do not test V7. It discusses related generalization research but does not use a listed claim as a tool.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: functional-topology summaries correlate with generalization gaps, and their estimator predicts test performance without test samples for the target network. Clarify that fitting and validating the regression uses measured training–testing gaps from other runs; the method is not developed without held-out performance information.
record.recipe_differences: Measures correlations between functional-topology summaries and the performance gap, then evaluates a gap estimator; it does not reproduce the original interventions or comparisons in the listed sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different prediction errors across tasks and validation schemes (leave-one-sample-out versus leave-one-dataset-out); it also uses different metrics for classification, facial action unit recognition, and segmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: Functional-topology cavity life and midlife have reported average correlations of −0.76 and 0.82 with the training–testing performance gap across the evaluated vision tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persistent-homology summaries of activation-correlation graphs correlate with generalization gaps in the evaluated networks and selected training runs.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear regressors using these summaries estimate held-out performance with task-dependent errors; Tables 1, 3 and 5 report leave-one-sample-out prediction errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A calibrated regression from functional-topology summaries can estimate test performance for the evaluated computer-vision networks.

record.problems: The paper reports aggregate correlations without uncertainty estimates. The displayed task-level error summaries are aggregate means and standard deviations; the text does not establish how well the estimator performs for each individual model beyond the tables and figures. Training uses validation performance to adapt learning rate, and available test sets are attached to training data for cross-validation.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported table entries omitted. Figures 5–7 show model- and dataset-specific plotted results but do not provide recoverable numeric values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width changes beyond the zero-training-error threshold and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under different tuning and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Topology correlations provide no verdict on sharpness. The reported correlations also concern selected runs: Section 5.5 restricts displayed results to performance above 50% and excludes extreme gaps. No additional version-bearing results were found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Widening beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-network performance.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the change in test accuracy.

relation.reason: The study discusses generalization and related predictors without testing the listed versions; cavity life and midlife do not measure V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness.

tranche.reason: Functional-topology correlations and gap-estimation results measure a related construct, but do not test or use any of V1–V8.

source_check.notes: The aggregate correlations are reported associations, not causal effects or evidence for V1–V8. Regression fitting and validation use measured training–testing gaps from other runs; reported results select runs exceeding 50% performance and exclude extreme gaps.
